candidates.title: Uber publishes its production security architecture for AI agents
candidates.summary: Uber described a three-layer production security architecture for first- and third-party agents, covering provisioning validation, runtime behavioral enforcement, and continuous assurance.
candidates.what_changed: The company published the operating architecture and implementation lessons behind its agent registry, automated code and tool analysis, semantic intent enforcement, prompt provenance, replay, red teaming, and per-agent calibration.
candidates.why_it_matters: The disclosure turns agent security from a list of guardrails into an inspectable lifecycle architecture, including the latency, false-block, developer-friction, and autonomy trade-offs encountered in production.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Treat agent behavior as a policy surface in addition to identity and authorization; define explicit intents and constraints, evaluate tool supply chains, and calibrate enforcement with shadow traffic and replay.

evidence.rationale: Uber's engineering team provides a first-party architecture and implementation account.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent measurement of control effectiveness was identified in this pass.
evidence.claim_scope: Architecture and reported operating lessons are first-party; the article does not publish universal effectiveness rates.

signal.rationale: The architecture materially affects how teams design agent identity, tool access, runtime enforcement, telemetry, and security review.

deduplication.canonical_event: Uber publishes its production lifecycle architecture for securing AI agents.
deduplication.material_delta: A new detailed first-party architecture and production lessons were published.

publication_verification.reason: The dated Uber engineering report supports the architecture and operating lessons; universal effectiveness is not claimed.

candidates.title: Kakao releases a small multimodal decision model for agent routing
candidates.summary: Kakao released Kanana-2-v-decide, a roughly 3B-parameter multimodal model that returns probability distributions for choices, yes/no questions, and ordered scores instead of generating prose.
candidates.what_changed: Weights, model documentation, and example usage became public for a decision-specific model accepting text, JSON, chat history, and up to ten images, with a 20,480-token input limit.
candidates.why_it_matters: A small non-generative model creates a distinct option for repeated routing and classification steps inside agents, where calibrated choices and latency can matter more than fluent text.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Evaluate the released weights on your own choice distributions, calibration, Korean and multimodal data, and license constraints before substituting it for a generative model or rules engine.

evidence.rationale: The weights and model card are public and the architecture and evaluation claims are documented by Kakao.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent reproduction of Kakao's latency or benchmark comparisons was identified.
evidence.claim_scope: Availability and interface are inspectable; speed and benchmark leadership remain vendor-reported.

signal.rationale: A decision-specific open model may change latency and control trade-offs for high-frequency agent routing.

deduplication.canonical_event: Kakao releases Kanana-2-v-decide weights and documentation.
deduplication.material_delta: A new public decision-specific multimodal model became available.

publication_verification.reason: The public model card and weights establish availability and interface; performance comparisons remain Kakao-reported.

candidates.title: A reliability framework shows why more agents do not guarantee a safer system
candidates.summary: A preprint combines imprecise-probability estimates for individual LLMs with a Bayesian network of multi-agent failure logic to produce system-level reliability envelopes.
candidates.what_changed: The authors applied the framework to a regulated chemical-hazard extraction pipeline and showed that majority voting protected against the weakest model but did not clearly outperform the best, while a 5% voter failure rate erased much of the advantage.
candidates.why_it_matters: Teams cannot infer system reliability from average model accuracy or agent count alone; the combining rule and deployment input mix become explicit failure contributors.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Model the voter, router, and operational profile as components with their own uncertainty instead of treating ensemble agreement as an automatic reliability gain.

evidence.rationale: The source is a current preprint with a concrete framework and case study, not peer-reviewed independent validation.
evidence.claim_scope: The reported envelope and case-study results support the narrower reliability lesson, not a universal ranking of ensemble designs.

signal.rationale: The work challenges a common architecture assumption and gives engineers a method for representing voter and workload uncertainty.

deduplication.canonical_event: The authors publish a system-level reliability-envelope method for multi-agent LLM systems.
deduplication.material_delta: A new reliability method and worked multi-agent case study were published.

publication_verification.reason: The arXiv record supports the method and case-study result; the work remains a preprint without independent reproduction.

candidates.title: GitHub adds API controls and attribution metadata for Copilot code review
candidates.summary: GitHub added REST and GraphQL controls for Copilot code-review settings plus attribution fields for reviews, effort metadata, and reported instruction, skill, and MCP sources.
candidates.what_changed: Enterprise, organization, and repository administrators gained API-managed review policy controls, while review output can now expose explicit provenance fields and reported configuration sources.
candidates.why_it_matters: Teams can automate review governance and audit which configuration surfaces influenced an AI review instead of relying only on web settings and opaque comments.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Inspect token and permission differences across enterprise, organization, and repository endpoints, then persist attribution and effort metadata with review evidence.

evidence.rationale: GitHub's dated changelog documents the shipped API and metadata changes.
evidence.independent_validation: The endpoints were not independently exercised in this pass.
evidence.claim_scope: Availability and documented fields are first-party; operational reliability improvements are not independently measured.

signal.rationale: Automatable policy and provenance materially improve how organizations govern AI-assisted code review.

deduplication.canonical_event: GitHub ships API-managed Copilot code-review settings and review attribution metadata.
deduplication.material_delta: New administrative APIs and review provenance fields became available.

publication_verification.reason: GitHub's dated changelog supports the API and metadata availability; the endpoints were not independently exercised.
